text: So, you want to play the best exclusive game available on your Xbox Series X, but within 47 minutes, you keep sliding all over the place, flying off the track, and most frustratingly won't stop crashing into goddamn walls. I'll admit it; driving in Forza Horizon 5 is really tough at first, but with a little help, you'll be winning races and clearing the map like the best of them.So, to help expedite the learning process here are a few quick tips and pieces of information so you too can become a Horizon superstar. Tip number one for you in this video is to comprehend that this game is not Mario Kart nor is it Need for Speed. Like in real life, you just can't try and drift at 170 miles an hour around a corner and expect it to work out.Both those games are designed so you almost never have to remove your finger from the gas pedal. Forza Horizon 5, while by no means a full-on simulation racer, does require you to drive and turn with much more care because of this having full control over your car is necessary in order to not only compete but to be able to finish races without crashing on almost every turn.That's why my biggest tip for you that I haven't seen mentioned in any other guides for this game is to play with manual shifting turned on. Now, I get it; the popular racing games outside of Forza have mostly been Need for Speed and Mario Burnout 64. But I'm telling you to get the most out of a game as refined as Forza Horizon 5 or any capital real racing game, for that matter, you gotta play with manual shifting.Not being able to manually downshift your car means it's almost impossible to throw the cars back out for turns without the use of the e-brake. And not being able to manually up shift means you're not optimally getting the car back up to top speed after slowing down for a corner. Believe me when I tell you that the jump from automatic to manual shifting will feel like a completely different game once you switch over.Manual shifting might seem like a Herculean task to learn, but you'll get the hang of it after only about 15 to 20 minutes of play. You use the X and B buttons on an Xbox pad to downshift and upshift respectively. Pay attention to the tachometer surrounding your speed in miles per hour. This along with the current speed of your car will tell you whether to either up or down shift.If the tachometer is revving up to about here, that's going to be the sweet spot to shift up to continue a smooth increase in speed. If you're driving in a high gear but the car is greatly slowed down, the car will still run, however it will take much longer to get your car back up to speed, which is where you'll want to downshift to help improve the acceleration of your car.If you listen to the roar of the engine and have controller vibration turned on, you can even hear and feel when it's time to change gears. While manual shifting requires more inputs and focus from you, shifting will quickly become second nature to you, and the amount of extra control you have over your car will be a huge boon in every single race you take on.Not to mention the game also gets way more fun. Speaking of races, let's actually get into some when doing races in Forza Horizon 5, you will see a big blue guiding line along the road that the race is on. For people new to racing games, this is not just used to help you navigate the courses while keeping your eyes on the road; this denotes the racing line or most optimal way to race around the course.While you're learning the game, stick to the racing line. You'll notice that the AI rigorously sticks the line as much as possible, so follow suit and deviate only when it's really time to make a pass. The racing line also tells you how fast you should be going by its color. Blue means that you're good to go and maintain your current speed.The color will fade from blue to yellow and then to red, which will tell you you need to lay on the break and slow down for the upcoming turn. As you play the game, you will slowly develop your own racing style, but here's what's helped me stick to the racing line.There are multiple ways you have to prepare your car for a turn. For slight turns, just taking your finger off the gas throttle for a second is all it takes. But for real corners, you're going to have to slow your car down. If you see the color of the line change back from yellow or red to blue, your speed is slow enough to cleanly follow the racing line through the turn.You might be someone like me when you first play this game and think that you need to drift around every corner like it's Daytona USA or Ridge Racer Type 4. And forza horizon 5, it's the exact opposite; you actually want to avoid going into a hard drift as much as possible. This is because the excess wheel spinning can really slow your car down, allowing for the drivers behind you to pass you, and there's no comeback mechanics like nitrous boost or item stuff.You get back to the front of the pack either way. The act of turning in Forza Horizon 5 is a balancing act between speed meeting clean maneuverability. A lot about turning comes from good instincts which you'll grow as you play. Moral of the game but making sure you're liberally using your brakes around corners and sticking to the racing line will help improve those instincts much faster.There are four primary racing disciplines in Forza Horizon 5: Road Racing is your classic officially sanctioned circuit, Sprint Races primarily take place on asphalt, Street Races are similar however there are always sprint events, and have regular NPC cars driving as hazards that need to be avoided and accounted for. Dirt Racing is just what it sounds like, racing primarily on dirt and off-road environments.Cross-country races are a mix of dirt and road racing with a lot more off-road hazards like having to drive through water and whatnot. Now while a car is only as good as its driver, that is; your car choice isn't going to affect your ability to win races. The good news is in Forza Horizon 5 the AI is always balanced to use cars of a similar class to whatever car you bring to an event.Meaning that in single-player, it's viable to win races with whatever you want. Whenever that's not to say that the card you picked might not be suited for the race of hand. For dirt and cross-country races, you want to pick a vehicle that can handle the off-road with ready tires and all-wheel drive to keep their grip against nature's racing courses.Meanwhile, Rear Wheel Drive cars are king for street and road races. You want to spend some time with the upgrade system in this game because driving a stock car will leave you with a lot to be desired. Thankfully every car in the game can be upgraded with new parts to greatly improve their performance capabilities.The class system is ranked into D, C, B, A, S1, S2 and X classes. While it might seem like a good idea to upgrade everything close to X, I'd recommend holding off on blowing your credits on that as typically raising some load to your beater more than two classes will leave the car being tough to control and still won't be able to compete with the better cars that just fall naturally in the higher classes.When you find a car you love, it's all about finding the right class that it can stay competitive in. For example, my beloved Ford Bronco is great for Dirt Racing and with the right upgrades can even do well on some of the faster tracks.Okay before we end the video here are some quick last-minute tips: You unlock the ability to fast travel by purchasing this property for 2 million credits. Get the story exhibitions done as soon as possible to start getting all other events and races to appear on the map.The rewind feature can rewind much further back than you think, you can use it to reset up your car in specific positions for open-world challenges like drift zones and speed traps. Speaking of rewinding, I mainly like to use rewind to practice tight turns and racing. Doing tight turns over and over will give you a good sense of when and how much you need to slow down your car to make it through.Inevitably, you'll get to a point where you no longer need to have the rewind on at all. Challenge yourself by increasing the difficulty of the AI and turning on more of the difficulty modifiers; some you won't even miss. It will make you more money from races, these race courses need to be learned.Don't be discouraged if you lose on your first race on the track. Course knowledge can better help prepare for knowing where hard turns are and what places in the track are optimal for passing. Staying in front of the AI is much easier than passing them once you're in first place, use the rearview mirror to see where second place is and block off their passes as they don't challenge your position too much.Finally, go to the design and car paint screen and put on an anime girl decal on your car; it'll make it go 12 miles per hour faster. That's all the tips I have for you in this video. I know a lot of these arcade sim racing games can come across as really intimidating if you're used to driving into other open-world games like GTA or Far Cry, but once you learn the intricacies of it, I think you'll find the active driving to be way more rewarding than anything found in those games.If you have a 4Z tip that I didn't mention, please drop it in the comments below and make sure to subscribe to Turnstyle for more guides reviews and other equally based gaming content. Take care!

Hello everyone, I'm AR for Speed. Today's video will teach you how to control your car better and perform well in cruising and other events. I previously did a video on controlling dead zones and driving, but I'm redoing it because I think it didn't fully reach out to its intended audience.So, we'll start with the cars. The first one is the hypercar - specifically, the Hennessy Venom F5. Let's hop in and see how it handles. If you're playing on automatic, this video isn't for you unless you plan to switch to manual mode later.When shifting gears, make sure they are in good working order. I have no assist turned on, only launch control enabled. Now, let's go through the settings: difficulty level, breaking traction stability, and driving line - all off except for launch control. This is a crucial step because some cars can be quite unpredictable.When driving normally or in a cruise event, keep your car in its highest gear to maintain speed. I'm currently shifting into lower gears too early, so let's avoid that. If you want to go 80-90 miles per hour, shift into the highest gear and hold down slightly on the gas pedal - this will help maintain speed without swerving or bumping into other cars.If there's a straightaway ahead, downshift to a lower gear, then back up to your highest gear once you've picked up more speed. Now let's say you're driving a manual transmission car with a clutch. In real-life cars like the Silverado or Kia Forte, you might not notice this as much because they are designed for comfort.However, when it comes to maintaining speed in a real car, shifting down into the nearest highest gear (or your highest gear) is crucial. Don't worry if you're new to driving manual - with practice, you'll see an improvement and be able to control your car better.Now let's move on to super cars. The process is pretty much the same as with hypercars, but keep in mind that some settings may affect performance. If you drive a manual transmission car with clutch, you'll notice it performs slightly better than driving an automatic. I might do a separate video just for this topic.If you're having trouble shifting gears smoothly, try practicing without assists turned on - this will help you develop your skills and fine-tune the settings to suit your style. Now let's move on to my next car, the Nissan Z. As usual, I won't be using any assistive features.Here we are at a festival with a bunch of people watching me drive. It's not too difficult when you get used to it - remember that different cars have varying torque ratios and handling characteristics, so don't worry if you're struggling at first.Keep in mind that even with the right tuning, this car is still quite torky, but I'm doing my best to maintain speed without oversteering. With practice, you'll develop a better feel for the controls and be able to drive more smoothly. That's all for today - hopefully, this video has been helpful in teaching you how to control your car like a pro!

Hey guys, so I got some tips for you on how to improve your driving and get faster lap times in Forza Horizon 5. I've played Forza Horizon 4 for about 600 hours and Ford's Horizon 5 for just over 240 hours, and recently made the switch from keyboard to controller, no assists.The first tip is, get rid of all the assists - yes, all of them, even ABS. I made a video where I talked about the assists and showed you all the differences, but I'll summarize it here if you don't want to watch that one. With ABS on or off, when you're not using ABS, you want to apply as much braking power as possible, not always necessary, I know. Sometimes you just want to tap the brakes, but let's say you have a big red braking line and you want to slow down as fast as possible over the shortest distance possible.Without ABS, if you apply maximum braking power without locking up the wheels, you're going to slow down faster, but if you lock up the wheels, the car is basically on ice. There's a fine line between not breaking enough or breaking too hard, and you're looking for that fine line each time you're braking.With ABS on, the wheels will lock up 50% of the time, which means you sacrifice braking power to be able to control the car. But what if you can control the car and apply 80 braking power? Wouldn't that be better? You might think it's too much effort for such little gain, but depends on how many braking zones we're talking about.Statistically, ABS off is faster. The next one is shifting manual plus clutch. I don't understand why some of you use manual without the clutch - it's not hard to press two buttons instead of one. Some cars require the clutch to be good, for example, the Mercedes X-Class. If you're still using automatic, switch to manual and get used to that.The clutch helps to shift faster, and this matters a lot in B-class or A-class steering simulation is a bit faster because standard has some sort of assisted elements. If you're using standard, switch to simulation, and you'll feel that the steering is more responsive.Stability control has the potential to slow you down a lot in corners if there's even the slightest sideways action. Traction control intervenes because you gave it too much gas - your fault for getting slowed down by traction control. Just slowly press the trigger or tap the key if you're on keyboard.Rivals as much as possible, story time. Ten years ago, I was playing CS:GO 1.6 and wanted to become good at the game, and one thing that helped me a lot was going on respawn servers - you die one second later, you're back and ready to rock and roll.In normal matches when you died, you had to wait for the round to finish. I know nowadays there are training maps and all that stuff, but translate rivals in 4005. Pick someone who's better than you, don't pick someone way faster than you because you want to be able to see which racing line he's taking how much he's braking.This leads me to my third tip: the blue racing line is sometimes wrong - heck, even the braking line is sometimes wrong, it's more of an AI path than a racing line. Get rid of it, keep the braking line though, most of the time it will help. Remember, just because it's red doesn't mean you can't take that corner flat out.Join a community where people share the same passion - there's a Forza Horizon 5 community on Steam. Stay away from that if you want to improve your driving. When someone says keyboard is better than controller for racing games or ABS is faster, they have no idea what they're talking about.I guess this is why competitive players use controllers and no ABS. I wouldn't recommend Reddit in general, especially the official subreddit which is flooded by screenshots. The official Forza Horizon forum is more for technical problems.What I would recommend is watching the best of the best on Twitch - for example, Nalak Dallas Mars Cod Cows. They'll answer any question about the game. These guys play on a controller, but if you're looking for someone who's good on keyboard, "I suck at driving" is your guy.This goes hand in hand with the previous one: learn how to tune. This applies to me as well - it's going to be quite an improvement when you manage to tune a car specifically for your racing style or for your needs.Let's take the 4GT as an example - you can have a tune for circuits and another one made for sprints. That 5-star tune that you downloaded is most likely not the fastest. Even some famous tuners make the car feel good but doesn't mean fast.Just take this list if you can be bothered to learn how to tune your own cars, and know that I trust most of these guys. For keyboard, we have Grandma Driving/Suck at Driving/Devoxx and Blue Cartel. I'm going to play a small clip here - I really don't care if it gets taken down or something, don't give a [expletive]. Quite incredible for me how you can finish lap like that - feels like one of the best laps you've ever done in your life, you're still in the scheme of things incredibly fast.But these guys have just got something more. Use the right car/tune for the track. I'm also going to provide two spreadsheets here, the links will be in the description. Another good way to find the best cars is rivals - open up the leaderboard for a specific track and see which car they're using.That's most likely the best car for that specific track. You need to be aware of certain game mechanics like slipstream and dirty air. Take advantage of slipstream on the straight, you're getting [expletive] by dirty air in corners in 4005. The slipstream effect is very weak on the other hand, dirty air in S2 is a real problem, and you'll have to compensate for that.Understeer engine braking - downshifting very fast while braking will slow down the car faster. Trail braking - braking during corner entry requires some skill. Wet penalty - basically certain cars get a penalty in wet conditions and they're not as good as they usually are in dry conditions.Record your gameplay, story time again. What helped me a lot getting to legend in Hearthstone was recordings - I was recording myself playing and then watching the videos to discover better moves.Record your gameplay and see where you're losing too much time, are you braking too much? Maybe you can discover a faster line, maybe you can carry a bit more speed through that corner. Maybe you're shifting up too early or too late when you're driving - you're not always aware of these things because well, you also have the opponents to worry about.But watching one of your races with a clear critical mind can help a lot. Probably doesn't apply to most of you but if you're playing on keyboard, consider switching to a controller. Want to know probably the best car for sprints in A-class? Dodge Dart - this damn thing is almost undrivable on keyboard.I have a video if you want to see the difference. Yet on controller, you can easily beat a very large portion of the player base like I said in the intro of this video. I'm making the switch at the moment because I've come to realize that keyboard is very limited and you're really wasting potential.What do I mean by limited throttle control and braking? And here we are - final tip: you've heard this numerous times, everyone is capable of giving you this tip, and it applies to all games and most things in life. Practice these guys who are at the top - it took them years to get there. If you're playing one hour per day, don't expect to be faster than someone who plays 5 hours a day.It's not reasonable at all. If you go to the gym one hour per day, sleep 6 hours and eat 3 times per day, don't expect to have better results than someone who works out 2 hours a day, sleeps 9 hours and eats 5 times a day. That person puts in more time and more practice than you - it's only fair they're better than you.Have a good one. Bye.

Welcome back to the channel, and today I'm going to teach you how to be faster in Forza Horizon 5 to beat your friends or a higher skilled difficulty driver.The first thing we're going to want to do is go into difficulty settings. Then, we're just going to go down through them. The first one is braking. You can have anti-lock on, which will assist you when you're braking coming into a corner. I don't have it on; I have it off because I want to tell the car when to brake, how much to brake, and whether I want the wheels to lock up or not.Next, we're going to go on to steering. I always use simulation steering. Then, we're going to do traction control and stability control. These should both be off at all times because traction control will cut the power to your wheels when it feels like the wheels are going to spin, and stability control will cut the power to your wheels when it feels like the car is going to spin. But I want to be the one to tell the car when I don't want power and when I do want power.Shifting - I know most of you will use automatic, but manual is far superior because it gives you a better rev range, and you can change the gear when you want. You can pick what gear you want to be in for what corner. So, you should be using manual.It's a steep learning curve, but once you've learned it, it is miles better than automatic. Manual with clutch is a different story completely; you shouldn't really be using that for racing. That's more for drifting around, if you want to drift, use manual clutch because you can do clutch kicking.Driving line - you should always use braking only if you want a bit more simulation, then take it off completely. But you should keep braking on because it will tell you when you need to brake, kind of. It's always in the wrong place, but it gives you a general idea that there's a big corner coming up.Because when you're driving fast against your friends, it is nice to have that little bit of help. So, you should keep that on.Really damaging tire wear - just turn it off; doesn't really matter. You can have it cosmetic if you want, but I just always have it off because I like the look of the car.Rewind - you can have rewind on if you want. I don't generally have it on, but for this purpose of the video, we've got it on. You can use it to give a bit more forgiveness, but when you're racing against your friends, you're not going to use it anyway because you're on an online race.That is the difficulty settings we're going to do next. We're going to show you proper racing lines in corners of how to get faster.Everybody can be fast in a straight line - that's not going to help you win a race unless you've got a stupidly powerful car compared to everybody else, but generally, you're not going to have that because you're driving against driver tires or other people who will have cars like you. The way you're going to win the race is through corners.Being fast through corners is where you will win any race online or against your friends. So, I've lined up two clips for you - on the left, it's as you would drive around when you're just playing around trying to be fast but not really trying, and then the one on the right is actual driving lines around the corner.Now you can see that the one on the right is 10 miles per hour faster than the one on the left straight away. You are much faster - 10 miles around the corner. If you add that up around every corner in the whole race, you're going to be miles ahead of any of your friends who are driving the other style.So, this is how you're going to win a race. Let's take a further look into it.What you want to do as you come into the corner is be as far to the apex on the right-hand side as possible to give you the best entry into the corner and exit out of the corner.The way we're going to do this is break as late as possible and as hard as possible without locking the tires up or losing traction. Then, once you've done that, you're going to do it at the start of the corner before you've even turned in.Then, you're going to let the brake off as you turn into the corner so you're not braking going around the corner. And then, as we're going around the corner, we're just going to hit the inside apex and then try and hit the outside apex.As you're coming out of the corner, put the power back on as slowly as you can to make sure that you don't lose grip but as powerful as you can to get at the most amount of speed coming out of the corner. And then you'll be faster than someone who is doing a Fast and Furious style right around the corner.This is how you are faster than your friends, and this is how you win races online in Forza Horizon 5.
